caption: Layer grouping patterns, where the horizontal and vertical axes represent groups (G_1, , G_4) and numbers of layers in groups.
model_annotation: The image illustrates five distinct layer grouping patterns for parameter-efficient fine-tuning design spaces, displayed as a horizontal sequence of five separate bar charts. According to the provided caption, the horizontal axis of each chart represents four sequential layer groups (arranged left to right as G_1 through G_4), and the vertical axis represents the number of layers within those groups. Neither axis features explicit vertical lines, tick marks, or numerical scales; instead, each chart indicates relative values using bar heights rising from a solid black horizontal baseline. Each of the five charts contains four contiguous, light green bars with black outlines corresponding to the four groups. The first chart, labeled "Increasing" below its baseline, features bars that progressively increase in height from the shortest bar on the far left to the tallest on the far right. The second chart, labeled "Uniform," displays four identically sized bars of equal height. The third chart, labeled "Decreasing," shows bars that progressively decrease in height, starting with the tallest on the left and ending with the shortest on the right. The fourth chart, labeled "Spindle," presents a symmetrical arrangement where the two outer bars are short and equal in height, while the two inner bars are taller and equal in height. The fifth chart, labeled "Bottleneck," features the inverse symmetrical layout, with the two outer bars being the tallest and equal in height, and the two inner bars being identically shorter. All bars share the same visual styling with no specific shading or annotations used for emphasis.
